text: At sunrise. <break time="0.8s" /> They gathered on a hill. <break time="0.8s" /> Where the chief put his cap on the ground. <break time="0.8s" /> As the starting mark. <break time="0.8s" /> Pahom walked east. <break time="0.8s" /> With a spade on his shoulder. <break time="0.8s" /> Digging holes along the way. <break time="0.8s" /> To mark his land. <break time="0.8s" /> Whenever he thought of turning. <break time="0.8s" /> He saw better land ahead. <break time="0.8s" /> And said. <break time="0.8s" /> It would be a pity to lose that. <break time="0.8s" /> When he finally turned toward the hill. <break time="0.8s" /> It was still ten miles away. <break time="0.8s" /> And the sun had begun to sink. <break time="0.8s" /> Throwing away his coat and boots. <break time="0.8s" /> He began to run. <break time="0.8s" /> And his heart beat like a hammer. <break time="0.8s" /> If I stopped now. <break time="0.8s" /> They would call me a fool. <break time="0.8s" /> He thought. <break time="0.8s" /> So he ran on although he could hardly breathe. <break time="0.8s" /> He reached the foot of the hill. <break time="0.8s" /> As the sun set. <break time="0.8s" /> But up on the hilltop. <break time="0.8s" /> It was still shining. <break time="0.8s" /> With his last strength. <break time="0.8s" /> He rushed up and fell forward. <break time="0.8s" /> Reaching the cap with his hands. <break time="0.8s" /> And the chief cried. <break time="0.8s" /> He has gained much land. <break time="0.8s" /> His servant ran up to lift him. <break time="0.8s" /> But Pahom was dead. <break time="0.8s" /> So the servant dug a grave. <break time="0.8s" /> With the spade. <break time="0.8s" /> Six feet from his head to his heels. <break time="0.8s" /> Was all the land. <break time="0.8s" /> That he needed.
